gloss: sweet bean paste; thick starchy sauce

definitions.gloss: sweet bean paste, red bean paste, filling (for wagashi)
definitions.explanation: Most commonly refers to sweet paste made from azuki beans, used in Japanese confections. Can be smooth (koshi-an) or chunky (tsubu-an).
Refers to thickened sauces used in Chinese and Japanese cuisine, often made with starch.

examples.japanese: この{大福|だいふく}には{餡|あん}がたっぷり{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: This daifuku is filled with plenty of sweet bean paste.

examples.japanese: {餡|あん}は{粒餡|つぶあん}と{漉|こ}し{餡|あん}のどちらが{好|す}きですか。
examples.english: Do you prefer chunky or smooth bean paste?

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{小豆|あずき}から{餡|あん}を{手作|てづく}りした。
examples.english: My grandmother made sweet bean paste from azuki beans by hand.

examples.japanese: {餡|あん}かけ{焼|や}きそばを{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
examples.english: I ordered fried noodles with thick sauce.

examples.japanese: とろみのある{餡|あん}が{料理|りょうり}に{絡|から}んで{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: The thick sauce coating the dish is delicious.

examples.japanese: {片栗粉|かたくりこ}で{餡|あん}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Make a thick sauce with potato starch.

notes:
{餡|あん} has two distinct meanings depending on context: sweet bean paste used in {和菓子|わがし} (Japanese confections), and savory thickened sauce used in cooking.

SENSE 1 — SWEET BEAN PASTE:
Made from {小豆|あずき} (azuki beans), this is the most common filling in Japanese sweets.

Types:
- {粒餡|つぶあん}: chunky bean paste (beans partially intact)
- {漉|こ}し{餡|あん}: smooth bean paste (strained)
- {白餡|しろあん}: white bean paste (from white beans)

Found in: {大福|だいふく}, {饅頭|まんじゅう}, {鯛焼|たいや}き, {羊羹|ようかん}

SENSE 2 — THICK SAUCE:
A starchy sauce made with {片栗粉|かたくりこ} (potato starch), used in Chinese-influenced Japanese dishes.
- {餡|あん}かけ: dish topped with thick sauce
- {餡|あん}かけ{焼|や}きそば: fried noodles with thick sauce

KANJI:
Also commonly written in hiragana as あん.
